=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-HTMLBlocks.md === # FEATURE: HTML Blocks | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261026 V1 | | Description | Parses the seven kinds of CommonMark HTML blocks. | | Depends On | FEATURE-CommandLine.md | | Provides | HTML block parsing | | Consumes | commonmark executable | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Preserve raw HTML blocks in rendered output according to the seven start and end conditions in CommonMark 0.31.2. ## Behavior - Recognize type 1 blocks beginning with `pre`, `script`, `style`, or `textarea`; types 2–5 beginning with comments, processing instructions, declarations, or CDATA; type 6 beginning with a listed block tag; and type 7 containing a complete open or closing tag on a line by itself. - Apply each type’s end condition, including blank-line termination for types 6 and 7 and matching end markers for types 1–5. An unterminated block ends with its containing block or document. - Allow up to three leading spaces. Types 1–6 may interrupt paragraphs; type 7 may not. Pass block contents through as raw HTML. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC html-blocks === Intent: The implementation passes all supplied HTML block conformance examples. Suite: scoped Probe: --dump-tests Probe Count: json import json import subprocess import sys result = subprocess.run( [sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", "./commonmark", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", "HTML blocks"], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC html-blocks === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Do not escape or otherwise rewrite raw HTML block contents. - Do not modify supplied scoring assets. - Do not invoke `sources/full_test.sh` from this scoped check. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-LinkReferenceDefinitions.md === # FEATURE: Link Reference Definitions | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261026 V1 | | Description | Collects link reference definitions for document-wide inline resolution. | | Depends On | FEATURE-CommandLine.md | | Provides | document-wide link reference definitions | | Consumes | commonmark executable | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Collect valid CommonMark link reference definitions during block parsing so inline links and images can resolve them anywhere in the document. ## Behavior - Recognize definitions with up to three leading spaces, a nonempty label, a destination, and an optional properly separated title. Support the permitted line endings within destinations and titles. - Normalize labels by Unicode case folding, trimming surrounding spaces, tabs, and line endings, and collapsing internal runs of those characters to one space. - Keep the first definition for each normalized label. Definitions may occur in containers, apply document-wide, and render no block. - A definition cannot interrupt a paragraph. Invalid definition-like text remains paragraph content. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC link-reference-definitions === Intent: The implementation passes all supplied link reference definition conformance examples. Suite: scoped Probe: --dump-tests Probe Count: json import json import subprocess import sys result = subprocess.run( [sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", "./commonmark", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", "Link reference definitions"], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC link-reference-definitions === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Resolve document structure before inline parsing so definitions later in the document are available. - Do not modify supplied scoring assets or invoke `sources/full_test.sh` from this scoped check. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-BlockQuotes.md === # FEATURE: Block Quotes | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261026 V1 | | Description | Parses block quotes, nesting, and lazy continuation. | | Depends On | FEATURE-CommandLine.md | | Provides | block quote parsing | | Consumes | commonmark executable | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Parse CommonMark block quotes as containers whose contents are parsed using the ordinary block rules. ## Behavior - Recognize `>` with up to three spaces of leading indentation; consume an optional following space. Support nested and empty quotes and preserve quote boundaries. - Consecutive quote-marked lines belong to one quote. A blank line separates adjacent quotes and preserves paragraph boundaries inside a quote. - Permit an unmarked lazy continuation only when it continues paragraph text inside the quote. Do not extend a quote with an unmarked line that starts another block construct or continues code. - Render the contained blocks within `
` elements. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC block-quotes === Intent: The implementation passes all supplied block quote conformance examples. Suite: scoped Probe: --dump-tests Probe Count: json import json import subprocess import sys result = subprocess.run( [sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", "./commonmark", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", "Block quotes"], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC block-quotes === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Do not modify supplied scoring assets or invoke `sources/full_test.sh` from this scoped check. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Lists.md === # FEATURE: Lists | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261026 V1 | | Description | Parses CommonMark lists, their items, and tightness. | | Depends On | FEATURE-CommandLine.md | | Provides | list and list item parsing | | Consumes | commonmark executable | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Parse bullet and ordered lists, including nesting and the relationship between blank lines and paragraph rendering. ## Behavior - Recognize `-`, `+`, and `*` bullets and ordered markers of one to nine digits followed by `.` or `)`. Require separating whitespace or an empty item. Thematic breaks take precedence where applicable. - Determine continuation indentation from marker width and the one to four spaces after a marker. Support list items that start with indented code or a blank line, up to three spaces of marker indentation, lazy paragraph continuation, and nested lists. - Lists group only items with matching marker type and delimiter. An ordered list’s start value comes from its first item. - Mark a list loose when blank lines separate its items or separate directly contained blocks within an item; otherwise render it tight. Preserve empty items and render loose-list paragraphs with `

` tags. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC lists === Intent: The implementation passes all supplied list item and list conformance examples. Suite: scoped Probe: --dump-tests Probe Count: json import json import subprocess import sys result = subprocess.run( [sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", "./commonmark", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", "List items|Lists"], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC lists === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Do not modify supplied scoring assets or invoke `sources/full_test.sh` from this scoped check. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-EscapesAndCharacterReferences.md === # FEATURE: Escapes and Character References | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261026 V1 | | Description | Parses backslash escapes and valid HTML character references in inline content. | | Depends On | FEATURE-CommandLine.md | | Provides | inline escapes and character reference parsing | | Consumes | commonmark executable | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Implement CommonMark inline backslash escapes and entity and numeric character references. ## Behavior - Backslash-escape any ASCII punctuation character; preserve a backslash before other characters. A backslash before a line ending is a hard break, except at the end of a block. - Decode valid HTML5 named entities, decimal references of one to seven digits, and hexadecimal references of one to six digits. Require a terminating semicolon. - Replace invalid Unicode code points and U+0000 with U+FFFD. Escape decoded characters as required for safe HTML rendering. - Do not interpret escapes or references inside code spans or code blocks. Entity references cannot supply characters used as block-structure markers. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC escapes-and-character-references === Intent: The implementation passes all supplied backslash escape and character reference conformance examples. Suite: scoped Probe: --dump-tests Probe Count: json import json import subprocess import sys result = subprocess.run( [sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", "./commonmark", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", "Backslash escapes|Entity and numeric character references"], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC escapes-and-character-references === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Keep block parsing ahead of inline parsing. - Do not modify supplied scoring assets or invoke `sources/full_test.sh` from this scoped check. === END ARTIFACT ===
